selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: A stage that replays after a backward jump must re-execute its own commands rather than reuse the previous run's results. The artifact-reuse decision for the replayed build-and-test stage is "Modify", not "Keep", because the loop-back repair changed the source under test: the suite grew from 65 to 66 tests, and T-FR3.3's verdict changed from Not Met to Met. Keeping the old results would have reported a defect that no longer exists.

selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: The `## Loop-Back Log` and the failure-ladder analysis are the one part of a failed run's artifact that must survive a replay verbatim. They are the diagnostic record that justifies the repair, so a re-run appends a resolution entry under the existing loop-back heading rather than replacing the section.

selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: The first run's target tally was wrong: it reported "36 applicable targets". 36 is the number of upstream ids in `traceability.json`, which includes the `FR1`–`FR5` group headings. The inventory's own "Applicable / Non-Applicable Determination" section states 31 leaf targets (24 FR + 7 NFR), all applicable, and the matrix carries exactly 31 rows. The replay corrected the tally to 31 and recorded the correction explicitly rather than silently restating it.

selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: Verifying a repair is not the same as verifying the code. The replay re-ran the whole build and test suite, the live per-state HTTP probe, and the live end-to-end smoke — and additionally reconstructed the pre-repair template branch in a throwaway copy of the project to confirm the new regression test genuinely fails against it. The mutation check is what distinguishes a test that pins the defect from one that passes regardless of implementation.

selections.heading: Corrections
selections.text: Chose to leave the two Minor documentation findings in `unit-test-instructions.md` uncorrected rather than re-open Plan Approval for a third round. That file is byte-bound by the code-generation approval fingerprint, so a two-line edit to a stale test count would invalidate the approval binding and cost another full approval round for a change with no effect on any command, threshold, or runtime behaviour. The authoritative counts live in `test-results.md` and `code-summary.md`.
